VII. Irreversible and Irretrievable Commitments of Resources Involved in the Proposed Action
Although not irreversible in a strict sense, it is acknowledged that areas opened or closed for ORV use will be difficult to change once use patterns are established.
Within designated ORV areas some irreversible or irretrievable impacts upon land forms, wildlife and their habitat, and historical and archeological sites may occur despite the utmost of precautions.
VIII. Consultation and Coordination in the Development of the Proposals and in the Preparation of the Draft Environmental Statement
The proposals evolved over a period of many months, following the issuance of Executive Order 11644 on February 8, 1972. In response to the Order, the Secretary of the Interior issued a Departmental memorandum on May 5, 1972, providing policies and procedures for implementing the Order on Interior lands.
Subsequently, the Department's draft ORV environmental statement was prepared and notice of its availability for formal review and comment was announced in the Federal Register, Volume 37, No. 107, pages 11078 and 11079, on June 2, 1972. Written comments were invited for a period of 45 days from the date of the notice. The announcement indicated locations where copies of the statement were available for inspection. Also, it indicated where copies of the statement could be purchased.
The Department has developed draft ORV regulations for implementing the Executive Order on Interior lands under the administration of the National Park Service, Bureau of Sport Fisheries and Wildlife, Bureau of Land Management, and Bureau of Reclamation. During the period between May 1972 and February 1973, these draft ORV regulations were reviewed by the involved Federal agencies, including the Office of Management and Budget. In February 1973, the Office of Management and Budget approved the Department's draft ORV regulations, and on February 14, 1973, these draft regulations and the notice of the reopening of the review period for the Department's draft ORV environmental statement (INT DES 72-62) were published in the Federal Register, Vol. 38, No. 30, pp. 4403-07 and 4421-22.
* Written comments were invited from all interested parties during the 60-day review period ending April 16, 1973. During this time, the Department held public meetings to provide additional information and to give the public an opportunity to comment on the draft ORV environmental statement and draft regulations.
